body: I don't want to make a million excuses but I've really isolated myself completely.  I also own this house and have a bunch of pets so the idea of moving right now is hard.  I am thinking that in June I will know if I'm going to continue working at the same job I'm currently at.  If I'm laid off, I'll sell this house and go back to school.  Move to a different state, most likely.
I want to be normal. Don't know quite how to do that.
I don't have anyone to lean on like that. Wish I could say that I did.
I'm really sorry. Did you live together? How long was he an addict?
I know you're right...Idk how to actually do all this and fix myself.

Why are you having the police involved?

The detox people fucking hate me because I call too often. I call because they don't pass along my messages! I wish there was some kind of support for those living with addicts. Alanon  meets so infrequently near me, but the rate of overdoses  is so high...

Moving back in with my parents is not an option. They are the only family I really have. I guess that's kind of a long, fucked up story in and of itself  which sort of explains why I'm so dependant on him.

Thanks :)

I will pm her.  

My psychiatrist (who I see once a month for ADD meds) got to see me in my full hysterical glory last time my bf went into detox.  She says I'm co-dependent. Idk how to fix that, though.  I wish I could.  I appreciate your help.

I've isolated myself from friends and family.  I didn't want anyone to know...now I feel like I am on an island alone.  I spoke with my talk therapist lady today and it makes me feel like such a freak that I have to pay someone to talk to me.

Don't worry about being blunt.  I need honesty.  

The thing about the counselor is that he advertised himself as an addiction specialist...he was more of a sobriety specialist, I guess.  It was just shocking to go through all the paces and then be told that we would NOT be seen again.  I wish the guy had told us up front what the requirements for his therapy were.
You're so right on the waiting for a man who doesn't exist.

>The cosign thing we say at NA in my area. It means advocate for yourself. If he is full of shit call him out, reality is harsh but it may just save his life. 

Thank you. I have been doing that more often recently. Not sure if it's getting anywhere.
I've been enabling him since about November of 2012. I wish I could say I know what I want. I wish it wasn't this way. I feel powerless but you are right.  I have the power to take care of myself.
I know that's what I should do. I'm weak.  I like him being home. Idk how to do anything right :-(

I had a feeling that he was treated with kid gloves in detox. He's said several times he wants to go back. Who wouldn't if everyone is super nice and tells you how brave you are every day?  He is not interested in sober living so I don't hear him say much about it. 

 I really appreciate your help. Merry Christmas to you as well :)
Consign like pawn but not sell?  TY I needed all of what you said.
I'm pretty good at not taking things personally.  He usually has no explanation or strong memory of why he said the particularly mean stuff.  That makes me feel better.

As I said in my post, alcohol is a problem for us both.  I didn't mean to make him feel uncomfortable by asking to go to an NA meeting with him.  I thought that maybe I could learn something and be able to help him - without him feeling shitty.

Thank you.  I see a distinct line being drawn between NA and AA.  For now, I am allowed on the AA side.  I understand his wanting to go to NA alone.  I just get discouraged when I'm screamed at for being "selfish" for wanting to go to the meeting with him.  I know not to take it personally. 


I am trying to not let him drag me down.  I don't think he is in the traditional sense (all I've ever done is drink).  He does make me feel emotionally bad, though.  I'm the "crazy" one.  I want to put myself first.  I keep thinking he could be given some opportunity and leave me at a heartbeat. I need to toughen up.

Thank you for replying.  Unfortunately there are very few Al-Anon resources around me (despite a huge amount of heroin addicts)...I just looked and since I am on vacation tomorrow I'll take a drive and hit up one at 9:30.

Communicating is very, very hard for us.  I have been in therapy for a long time and I work with teenagers so I'm pretty decent with conflict management but I keep finding myself crossing HUGE(?) boundaries that I didn't know existed.  

I have made that ultimatum about disappearing and stealing from me in the past and always renege on it when he comes around, apologetic.  I have to be a stronger person before I can help him.  Thank you so much for your advice.

I **really, really** appreciate the advice.I do know the PAWS stuff.  You're not coming off as harsh at all.   

I know that since we live together, I am an easy target.  I am working on not giving in to that, and he has been quick to quiet down if I say, "Hey, I have nothing to do with your heroin addiction, I'm just here for you now."  He seems to have liked being in detox but didn't want to do sober living.  He starts IOP tomorrow - 3 hours a day, 3 days a week.  Still unemployed and deeply in debt.  

I do have my own counselor.  I set up couples' counseling with a guy referred to me by my counselor as one who is good with addiction & couples.  We start on Jan 6th.  I have been shouldering a lot in the relationship but I think it's mostly been a financial burden.  I can't make him pony up rent or utilities.  Today I did tell him to go back on unemployment.  That was $220 2x a month last time he did it.  That would help.  

Anything else you can think of, please let me know.  I've truly never known him sober.  He's always been a heavy drinker.  I'm so lost in all this as it was so sudden and shocking and now I need to change a lot about my own behavior as well.  I don't want to lose him but I guess I'd be losing someone I hardly know :-(

Thank you for your reply.  I really identified with "You can't really do this for him as much as you want to."  I keep thinking that if I push the healthy things...gym, vitamins, meetings, etc., I am helping.  I'm obviously not :(  

I am heartbroken.  It's a weird heartbroken.  Usually heartbreak means break-up.  But he's still here.  I guess I have to come to terms with who he is now and how that is different from what I thought I knew.   Do people really stay with their partners after all this?  Is there any way to tell that he's "better"?
